To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cascade equations are a useful tool in the study of air showers.

a hybrid method for the simulation of extensive air showers can be developed, that this method is computationally more efficient than pure Monte Carlo methods, that it reproduces all the relevant physical features of air showers and that the lateral distributions of the particles in the shower can be simulated accurately.
the cascade equations provide an efficient and accurate way to simulate air showers at energies below the knee of the primary cosmic ray spectrum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hybrid method for air shower simulations.
the simulation of extensive air showers in the atmosphere.
the development of a simulation technique which is accurate, flexible, and efficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new method is superior to the traditional approach in all respects except for the most accurate determination of the total number of electrons at high energies.
the hybrid method is a very efficient way to simulate extensive air showers.
the new hybrid approach provides a very efficient method of shower simulation, with the accuracy of a Monte Carlo method and the speed of a cascade approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to reproduce the results from the CORSIKA simulation program with a factor of 1000 less computing time.
we have developed a new simulation procedure which is applicable over a wide range of energies.
this hybrid method is the most efficient and accurate method for air shower simulations at present.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cascade equations are very accurate in describing the development of the shower in its initial phase, and can be used with great success for air shower simulations at very high energies, where they are applicable.
it is possible to simulate showers in a hybrid approach, which combines the advantages of the cascade equations and the Monte Carlo method.
the cascade equations are very accurate and that they provide a natural bridge between the high and low energy regimes in air shower simulations.
